/-!
# Erdős Problem 466

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/466](https://www.erdosproblems.com/466)
- [Er72] Erdős, Paul, *Extremal problems in number theory*. Proceedings of the 1972 Number Theory
  Conference (Univ. Colorado, Boulder, Colo.) (1972), 80-86.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved*. (1982),
  59-79.
- [Sa76] Sárközy, A., *On distances near integers. I, II*. Studia Sci. Math. Hungar. (1976), 37-50,
  105-111.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Metric

namespace Erdos466

/--
`N X δ` is the maximum number of points in a closed disc of radius `X` in the plane such that
the distance between any two of them is at least `δ` away from the nearest integer.
-/
noncomputable def N (X δ : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {n | ∃ (c : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) (P : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
    P.card = n ∧ ↑P ⊆ closedBall c X ∧
      (P : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))).Pairwise fun x y => δ ≤ distToNearestInt (dist x y)}

/--
Let $N(X,\delta)$ denote the maximum number of points $P_1,\ldots,P_n$ which can be chosen in a
circle of radius $X$ such that
$$\| \lvert P_i-P_j\rvert \| \geq \delta$$
for all $1\leq i<j\leq n$. (Here $\|x\|$ is the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer.)

Is there some $\delta>0$ such that
$$\lim_{X\to \infty}N(X,\delta)=\infty?$$

Graham proved this is true, and in fact $N(X,1/10)> \frac{\log X}{10}$. This was substantially
improved by Sárközy [Sa76], who proved that for all sufficiently small $\delta>0$,
$N(X,\delta)>X^{1/2-\delta^{1/7}}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 52, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos466.lean#L292"]
theorem erdos_466 : answer(True) ↔ ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ Tendsto (fun X ↦ N X δ) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/-- Graham proved that $N(X,1/10)> \frac{\log X}{10}$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 52]
theorem erdos_466.variants.graham : ∀ X : ℝ, 1 ≤ X → Real.log X / 10 < N X (1 / 10) := by
  sorry

/--
Sárközy [Sa76] proved that for all sufficiently small $\delta>0$,
$N(X,\delta)>X^{1/2-\delta^{1/7}}$ for all sufficiently large $X$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 52]
theorem erdos_466.variants.sarkozy : ∃ δ₀ : ℝ, 0 < δ₀ ∧ ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → δ < δ₀ →
    ∀ᶠ X : ℝ in atTop, X ^ (1 / 2 - δ ^ (1 / 7 : ℝ)) < N X δ := by
  sorry

end Erdos466

reformulations.difference: The source describes a maximum cardinality; Lean takes a natural-number supremum of admissible finite-set cardinalities.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For δ > 0, every admissible pair has Euclidean distance at least δ, since distance to the nearest integer is at most distance to 0. Translating the disk to the origin and covering it by finitely many open balls of radius δ/2 bounds all admissible cardinalities. The cardinality set is nonempty, so its natural-number supremum is attained and is its maximum. All three theorems use positive δ. The scratch file proves both attainment and `N X δ = n ↔ IsGreatest (sizes X δ) n`.

reformulations.difference: Lean states the displayed logarithmic bound only for X ≥ 1, rather than for every positive radius.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For 0 < X < 1, log X / 10 < 0 ≤ N(X,1/10), so the omitted positive-radius cases hold automatically. The universal formulations over X ≥ 1 and X > 0 were proved equivalent in the scratch file.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, Extremal problems in number theory (1972), §IV, p. 83: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1972-05.pdf
P. Erdős and R. L. Graham, Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory (1980), pp. 92–93: https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf
P. Erdős, Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved (1982), §9, pp. 67–68: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1982-33.pdf

A. Sárközy, On distances near integers, I and II, Studia Scientiarum Mathematicarum Hungarica 11 (1976), especially Part I p. 37 and Part II pp. 105–107, Theorem 1: https://real-j.mtak.hu/5461/1/StudScientMath_11.pdf

review.notes: All four declarations were checked; no mathematical defect or status discrepancy was found. The live erdosproblems.com page returned a Cloudflare challenge, so comparison used the cited primary publications instead. Sárközy's Theorem 1 confirms the exponent and the δ-dependent sufficiently-large-X quantifier. Scratch checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile without errors, including N(0,δ)=1, negative-radius values, and N(X,δ)=1 for X≥0 and δ>1/2. The cited external proof also compiles with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound; its indexed-point definition was proved equivalent to the file's finite-set definition.
